turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response:
Well, hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place. I don't want to take up too much of your time, but... well, my supervisor at the building where I clean, he sort of suggested I come in. 

It's just a little thing, really, nothing too bad, but... sometimes my talking gets a bit, well, mixed up, I guess? Like, I'll be trying to explain something simple, you know, about the building keys, and then... I don't know, it just flows into talking about the jail, and then my prayer rug, and then maybe the chess pieces... and people, they tell me they just can't follow what I'm saying. I try my best to be clear, I really do, but it just comes out all jumbled sometimes. Is that... is that something you can help with, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient describes their speech getting mixed up and jumbled, jumping between unrelated topics (keys, jail, prayer rug, chess pieces) to the point where others cannot follow what they are saying.

turns.doctor_question: When your speech gets jumbled like that, does it feel like your thoughts are moving very fast, almost faster than you can speak them? Or does it feel more like you're having trouble organizing or finding the right words?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, that's a really good question, Doctor. Um... I think it's the first one. They're just moving so, so fast. I hope it's okay to explain it like this, but... it's not that I don't know the words, I promise I try my best to be organized. 

It's just that my thoughts run so fast, it almost feels like... well, like a whole crowd of people talking inside my head all at once? I mean, not in a bad or scary way, just... very busy. My mind will be jumping from worrying about my bills, to... to the jail, and then over to the mosque, and then right into the cleaning chemicals I need for the third floor... and it all happens before I can even catch one single thought to say it out loud properly. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.

symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient explicitly confirms that their thoughts are moving very fast, describing them as jumping rapidly between multiple topics before they can catch a single thought.

And it's not like a thought, Doctor, it sounds just as real as you talking to me right now. He calls my name, or... or sometimes he tells me that I ruined everything. 

I try not to let it bother me, I really do. I just keep my head down and keep cleaning. But it does feel very real. Is... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to be honest so you can help me, but I hope I didn't say the wrong thing.

Like the way the hallway lights would flicker when I walked by, or the way the other workers would give each other these tiny little looks when I came into a room. I was just so sure they had marked me, you know? Like they were warning each other about me. 

My supervisor, he's a very nice man, he even showed me the security camera footage to prove there was nothing going on. And I know I should have just listened to him, because he's the boss and he knows best, but... I still felt so sure about it. Even after he showed me. 

I know that probably sounds very strange, Doctor. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad person. I just get so confused sometimes. Am I answering your question the right way? I really want to be helpful.
